title: When Do Intrinsic Rewards Lead to Exploration?
abstract: arXiv:2610.02159v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Intrinsic rewards are designed to guide exploration in reinforcement learning by assigning value to an agent's experience, for example through prediction error or learning progress. However, maximizing these rewards need not produce the most informative experience available. We propose a formal criterion for exploration that compares policies by the counterfactual information they acquire: how well their histories can substitute for experience under alternative policies. We construct a single, simple environment in which specified count-based, prediction-error, empowerment, and information-gain objectives have maximizing policies that are Pareto-suboptimal at acquiring counterfactual information. translated_title: 内在奖励何时能引导探索？
translated_abstract: 内在奖励旨在通过为智能体的经验赋予价值来引导强化学习中的探索，例如通过预测误差或学习进度。然而，最大化这些奖励并不一定产生可获得的最具信息量的经验。我们提出了一个关于探索的形式化准则，通过策略所获取的反事实信息来比较各策略：即策略的历史能在多大程度上替代其他策略下的经验。我们构建了一个单一的简单环境，在该环境中，指定的基于计数、预测误差、赋权和信息增益等目标的最大化策略在获取反事实信息方面是帕累托次优的。我们解释了这些失败的原因，并确立了现有内在奖励在何种条件下能够成功鼓励最优探索。我们还构建了一个目标函数，只要探索在我们的准则下有严格改进，该目标就会赋予更高的价值。
tldr: 论文提出了以反事实信息获取为核心的形式化探索准则，证明常见的内在奖励（基于计数、预测误差、赋权、信息增益）在特定环境中会导致帕累托次优的探索，并揭示了现有内在奖励成功引导最优探索所需的条件。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a formal exploration criterion based on counterfactual information acquisition, demonstrates that common intrinsic rewards (count-based, prediction-error, empowerment, and information-gain) can yield Pareto-suboptimal exploration in a specific environment, and establishes the conditions under which existing intrinsic rewards successfully encourage optimal exploration.
